runs.text: A program is a text with
a single algorithm
and, around it, the pieces that algorithm uses: subprograms, classes, records, enumerations and constants.
How it works
The top level of the text only accepts
units
: named blocks that open and close. No executable statement may be left loose outside them.

blocks.description: A file with four sibling units one under the other: the constant SALUDO, the enumeration Color, the algorithm Tienda, highlighted as the only one, and the subroutine Precio.

caption.text: A file with its single algorithm and its sibling units. None goes inside another, and order does not matter.

runs.text: Units are
siblings
: none goes inside another. They can be written before or after the algorithm, in any order.

blocks.title: An algorithm with its neighbours

runs.text: An empty algorithm is valid and does nothing. The algorithm's name does not take up the variable namespace: it may match the name of a variable.
Classic pseudocode
A program written in the classic style —
with several names,
, loops,
and
with a result variable— is analysed
without any diagnostic
and runs as is, also from the terminal with
. The only requirements are the usual ones: semicolons, indices from zero and no variable read without a value.
A statement outside every unit belongs nowhere:

diagnostics.message: Unexpected token outside algorithm and subroutines: Write

runs.text: And a text cannot have two algorithms:

blocks.title: Two algorithms in one text
blocks.source:
Algorithm Uno
EndAlgorithm
Algorithm Dos
EndAlgorithm

diagnostics.message: Multiple algorithms in a single source file are not allowed

points.text: A text has exactly one algorithm.
Sibling units go around it, in any order.
There are no loose statements or nested units.
